title: TON: on-delay timer
summary: TON switches its output Q on after its input IN has been TRUE continuously for the preset time PT. Q goes off immediately when IN goes off.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.body:
- While **IN** is FALSE, **Q** is FALSE and **ET** (elapsed time) is 0.
- When IN becomes TRUE, ET starts counting.
- When ET reaches **PT**, Q becomes TRUE and ET stays at PT.
- When IN becomes FALSE, Q and ET reset immediately.

An IN pulse shorter than PT never sets Q.

sections.heading: Example: delayed motor start
In PLC Lab
sections.body: Timers run on **simulation time**, never on the wall clock: pausing the simulation pauses the timer, and running at 500 % speed elapses the timer five times faster in real time but exactly as long in simulated time. ET advances by the cycle time once per scan.

inputs.name: IN
inputs.description: Start condition; timing runs while TRUE

outputs.name: Q
outputs.description: TRUE once IN has been TRUE for PT

instruction.state: Instance holds start time, elapsed time and output state.
instruction.retentivity: Not retentive; reset by a memory reset and by STOP-to-RUN restart in PLC Lab.
instruction.timing: Evaluated once per call; resolution equals the cycle time in PLC Lab.
